archiveTake: A slow-burning supernatural mystery where every answer only makes the whole thing more unsettling.
spoilerFreeReview: The White Vault is strong in that every answer leaves you with more questions. It's an unending mystery filled with supernatural occurrences. It finds a really good balance between leaving things just strange enough that you want to know what happens next without making the listener confused.

One thing I really liked was the international cast. There are voice actors from all around the world speaking all kinds of different languages. I at least got very happy when I heard my own native language, Swedish, being spoken. For people who only speak English, though, it's no problem. The show is intended for English speakers, and anything that isn't translated is usually either not important or simply not meant to be understood. This is something I've noticed in other Fool & Scholar shows too, since they often make use of international casts and characters.

I also really liked the found-footage style of storytelling. I usually dislike that format, but The White Vault does it incredibly well. It doesn't feel like you're gathering a bunch of separate pieces, it feels more like you're experiencing the whole story through them. I especially liked the variety of material, ranging from video and audio recordings to hastily written notes.
I would recommend this to anyone who wants a mystery where every answer only reveals something deeper, and the further down you go, the more unsettling it becomes.
thoughts: What surprised me most about The White Vault is how well the found-footage format works. I usually struggle with that style because it can feel fragmented, but here all the recordings, notes, and different perspectives still feel like parts of one continuous story.

I also really appreciate how international the cast feels. Hearing characters naturally switch between languages makes the world feel much more real, and hearing Swedish show up was a particularly fun surprise for me.
